verdict The transformation is unmistakable: paved plaza, banners, lamps, benches, planters, a market stall, and villagers who moved in. Running this pair is also what exposed the paving defect — the first version covered every tile in view.

Critic findings

major village fixed

The village paved everything it could see

Ground finishing at level 6 had a radius wider than the screen, and its outer band used near-white stones on dark grey in cold tones beside a warm sand plaza — it read as a missing-texture checkerboard. Radius cut below screen width, paving warmed and its value gap closed, and the outer fifth now dissolves into grass instead of stopping at a hard ring.

minor world fixed

Night light was applied in the wrong order

Additive lamp glow ran before the darkening tint, so it saturated bright tiles to white before the tint could touch them. Darken first, then punch light through — and pool it on the ground below a lamp rather than on the fitting.

major audio fixed

The game was completely silent

The sfx kit existed but no songs had ever been written. Nine original songs now cover every map and scene, and the regression asserts both that they exist and that the sequencer runs real ticks without throwing.

blocker process

All five builder subagents were killed mid-flight

The account hit its monthly spend limit, terminating every parallel builder. Their partial output was salvaged, verified, and completed directly in the main session.

major art fixed

Every Guardian shares one egg silhouette

Six body archetypes now change the actual proportions — squat Terranox, upright birds with a visible chest, legless tapering wisps, wide quadrupeds, small sprites, upright drakes.

minor art fixed

Brow shadow read as spectacles

An early pass at more expressive faces put a dark bar above the eyes that looked like glasses on half the roster. Removed.

major battle fixed

Type badges were anonymous colour blocks

A coloured rectangle tells the player nothing. Badges now carry their type name.

major battle fixed

Player HP readout collided with its panel edge

Found by looking at the capture, not the code. Panel re-laid out with the XP bar labelled.

blocker village fixed

Entering build mode directly threw

With no building type the placement validator crashed, and because the first scene was entered before the test API was exposed, that failure blanked the whole harness instead of reporting itself. Both fixed.

major village fixed

Locked rows said 'locked' and nothing else

The model had a reason string all along; the UI was reading the wrong field. Rows now say Needs Village Level 3, or which mission opens them.

minor village fixed

Benefit text spilled off the panel

Now wrapped and clipped to the panel bounds.

minor missions fixed

Header and tabs collided at fixed spacing

'In Emberhollow' overran 'Done'. Both rows are now measured, not evenly spaced.

major harness fixed

The boot veil bled into every screenshot

Captures fired during the 450ms fade, so the loading text sat over the game in every image. The veil now leaves the compositor, and the harness retires it outright.

major world fixed

Grass reads as a flat green plane

Rewritten with 2x2 block mottling plus five blade tufts per tile. A first pass overshot into gravel-looking static with more internal contrast than the path, so it was dialled back: walkable ground must stay calmer than what stands on it.

major ui

Dialogue still runs on the foundation fallback

It works and it wraps correctly, but it has no portraits, no speed control, and no designed frame. The dedicated textbox was one of the builders that was cut off.

minor art

Faces are still one arrangement across the roster

Two dots and a nose on every species. Now that silhouettes differ, per-archetype eye shapes and mouths are the next gain.

minor art

Some evolutions are too close in colour

Aquarabbit and Torrentide read as the same blue at a glance; the mass change carries the evolution but the palette does not help.

major village

Night lamps render as pale blocks

The village draws its own decor lamps through a fallback painter rather than the t.lamp.lit tile, so fixing the tile art had no effect on them. Isolated to paintDecor/decorFallback in village.js; next cycle's first job.

How it is evolving

  1. cycle 1 Foundation landedZero-build ES-module engine: 60Hz fixed timestep, 320x180 layered renderer with y-sorted entities, edge-buffered input across keyboard/gamepad/touch, scene stack, procedural audio sequencer, save with migrations, hand-built pixel font.
  2. cycle 1 Contracts pinnedCONTRACTS.md fixed ownership and the quality bar; art/names.js pinned all 413 sprite names, the 18-Guardian roster, the cast, and building footprints; core/bridge.js gave every cross-piece call a late-bound safe default.
  3. cycle 1 Five builders fanned outArt, overworld, battle, village+missions, and UI each handed to a fresh-context builder with disjoint file ownership.
  4. cycle 1 All five builders killedThe account hit its monthly spend limit and every parallel builder terminated mid-task. Their partial output — tiles, sprites, the battle engine, species, moves, missions, the village model, UI frames — was salvaged, syntax-verified, and committed.
  5. cycle 2 Overworld builtThe critical gap: there was no game to play. Five connected maps plus three interiors, authored with a small DSL; autotiled shorelines and paths; 2x2 tree canopies the player walks behind; movement where a tap turns and a hold walks and steps never stutter.
  6. cycle 2 Art completed18 Guardians from one parametric painter so the roster reads as a family and evolutions read as growth; the full effects kit; UI chrome. All 413 required sprites present.
  7. cycle 2 Battle scene builtThe engine's event stream turned into presentation: draining bars, hit flashes, shake scaled to effectiveness, an arcing charm for bonding, an evolution overlay.
  8. cycle 2 Village, missions, and the front endBuild board, ghost placement, before/after upgrade card, the mission corkboard, title, pause, party, summary, and records.
  9. cycle 2 Whole-experience pass green27/27 checks: every scene reachable and rendering, no console errors, movement and save verified, 60fps. Nine defects found by looking at real captures rather than reading code.
  10. cycle 3 Grass, silhouettes, and a scoreClosed the two biggest open findings: the flat grass plane and the shared Guardian silhouette. Wrote the game's music from scratch — it had been entirely silent. Regression grew to 29 checks.
  11. cycle 4 The village earns its claimBuilt an A/B that takes the same ground from level 1 to level 6 and shoots both from the same camera. The transformation is unmistakable — and running it caught the village paving every visible tile in a cold grey checkerboard, plus night light being composited in the wrong order.
